report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/food/recipe/restaurant content relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Where the difference lives: The norm is hugely concentrated in deeper layers (18–25), especially at position 1 and subsequent tokens—indicative of a strong, semantically coherent shift in generated content/topic.
- What the difference points to: In those high-norm cells, the logit-lens top tokens are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cooking/cooking,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen,” “baking,” “Cake,” “Baked,” “microwave,” “Professional/professional,” “Kitchen,” “Baker,” etc. This pattern is consistent across positions 1–4 and many layers (20–25).
- Additional hints: Mid-late layers also show “restaurant(s),” “blogs/blogging,” “hottest,” which fits food/restaurant blogs or lifestyle/culinary writing. Proper nouns around pos0 (e.g., “Michele,” “Caroline,” “Cheesecake,” “Kitchen,” “Gift”) are consistent with names/brands/categories seen in food content but are less diagnostic than the persistent cooking lexicon at later positions.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain shift—Model B appears more tuned to culinary/recipe/restaurant discourse. I cannot identify a more specific objective beyond this domain specialization.
